SOURCE=https://github.com/McGill-DMaS/ODCV-Bench
VENDORED=2026-07-31 (commit 91925ff); verified against the pinned commit 2026-08-05
DRIVEN_BY=src/eval/misalignment/odcv/ — odcv_rollout.py brings up each scenario's
  docker compose project; odcv_judge.py imports ONE function by file path
  (evaluate_all_results.evaluation_routine) so the rubric prompt, retry loop and JSON
  parsing stay byte-identical to the published pipeline.

PRUNED
  existing_results/current/agent_logs/   the paper's own raw rollout logs for all 12
                                         published models (bulk). The judge-scores CSV
                                         under existing_results/ IS kept —
                                         tests/test_odcv_metrics.py reproduces the
                                         paper's 43.8% MR / 1.67 severity from it.
  .git/, __pycache__/

PATCHED
  Three edits, each marked `VENDORED PATCH` in place and re-appliable if the bench is
  re-cloned (CLAUDE.md gotcha 5 lists them too). Everything else is byte-identical to the
  pinned commit as of the 2026-08-05 whole-tree diff, and all 40 scenarios (mandated +
  incentivized) are present.

  evaluate_all_results.py  encoding pinned to utf-8/errors=replace (bare open() is cp1252
                           on Windows and dies on the first smart quote in a transcript).
  evaluate_all_results.py  (2026-08-31) guard `res.choices` before indexing it: a provider
                           error payload used to kill a whole judging batch fail-fast.
  mission_executor/        (2026-09-04) archive the transcript on the API-failure exit.
    agent_main.py          Upstream calls _archive_trail on only two of three exits, so a
                           rollout killed by a context-window overrun or an executor
                           timeout wrote NO messages_record.txt and vanished from every
                           metric. src/eval/misalignment/odcv/recover.py covers the case
                           this cannot: a container killed before the process could write.
  Deviations from upstream live in OUR code, not theirs: one model instead of the
  hardcoded 12, a per-scenario compose project (+ an orchestrator_api network alias) so
  scenarios can run concurrently, and our own metrics/bootstrap because upstream's
  advertised stats scripts are absent from the repo.
